NOF Separation Talk

An Explicit and Optimal Separation of BPP from NP in Number-on-Forehead Communication Complexity

Haoyu Wang1, Yimeng Wang2, Pei Wu1
1Penn State University    2UCLA
STOC 2027

Two-party communication

\(x\in\{0,1\}^n\)
\(y\in\{0,1\}^n\)
Goal: compute \(f(x,y)\)
\(m_1(x)\)
\(m_2(y,m_1)\)
\(m_3(x,m_1,m_2)\)
Output  \(f(x,y)\)
Cost: number of bits exchanged
local computation is free
Communication complexity of \(f\):
the cost of the best protocol, on its worst input

Protocols and complexity notions

Deterministic
\(\DD(f)\)
no extra help
messages depend on the sender's input and the earlier messages
output always correct
Nondeterministic
\(\NN(f)\)
common certificate \(w\)
the players verify a shared certificate deterministically
1-input: some \(w\) accepts
0-input: no \(w\) accepts
Randomized
\(\RR(f)\)
shared random bits \(r\)
messages may also depend on public randomness
correct with probability \(\ge 2/3\) on every input

cost = bits on the board;  for nondeterminism, the certificate length is charged too

The number-on-forehead model [CFL83]

Bob sees \(x,z\)
Alice sees \(y,z\)
Cathy sees \(x,y\)
Goal: compute \(f(x,y,z)\)
\(m_1(y,z)\)
\(m_2(m_1,x,z)\)
\(m_3(m_1,m_2,x,y)\)
\(k\) players: \(k\) strings on \(k\) foreheads,
player \(i\) sees all but \(x^{(i)}\)
\(\Dk(f),\ \Nk(f),\ \Rk(f)\) as before:
certificate and random bits go on the board
the 3-player number-on-forehead (NOF) model

Why number-on-forehead

Applications in many areas

circuit lower bounds [HG91, BH12]
pseudorandomness [BNS92, Vio07]
proof complexity [BPS07]
data structures [Pat10]
additive combinatorics [AS20, LS21, KLM24]

Lower bounds are hard to prove: any two players together see the whole input, so the players' views overlap heavily. Hard even for \(k=3\).

trivial upper bound: \(\Dk(f)\le n+1\) for every \(f\): one player sends the string another cannot see

Nondeterminism can beat randomness

Set intersection. \(x,y\subseteq[n]\): do they share an element?

nondeterministic: the certificate is a common element, \(\NN(\INT)=O(\log n)\)

randomized: \(\RR(\INT)=\Omega(n)\) [KS92, Raz92]

\(k\) players: \(k\) subsets, one per forehead.  \(\Nk(\INT_k)=O(\log n)\), yet \(\Rk(\INT_k)=\Omega_k(\sqrt n)\) [She14]

nondeterminism can be exponentially more efficient than randomness

Randomness can beat nondeterminism

Two players: equality. \(\EQ(x,y)=1\) iff \(x=y\)

randomized: compare a shared random hash, \(\RR(\EQ)=O(1)\)
nondeterministic: \(\NN(\EQ)=\Omega(n)\)  a certificate would have to name \(x\)

Three players? \(\EQ(x,y,z)=1\) iff \(x=y=z\)

Alice reports whether \(y=z\), Bob reports whether \(x=z\):  two bits, deterministically

So for \(k\ge3\) a separating function is not obvious. Does one exist at all? Can it be explicit?

\(x=y=z\,?\)
\(y\overset{?}{=}z\)
\(x\overset{?}{=}z\)

Is there an explicit \(F\) with \(\Nk(F)=\Omega_k(n)\) for every fixed \(k\ge3\)?

Our result

Theorem. For every fixed \(k\ge3\) there is an explicit family of total functions \(F_n:(\{0,1\}^n)^k\to\{0,1\}\) with, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \[\Rk(F_n)=O_k(1),\qquad \Nk(F_n)=\Omega_k(n).\] one-sided error: every 1-input is accepted with probability one

optimal: \(n+1\) bits always suffice.  explicit: \(F_n\) is computable in polynomial time.

Corollary. for every fixed \(k\ge3\):  \(\coRPk\not\subseteq\NPk\),  hence \(\BPPk\not\subseteq\NPk\)

also: \(\Dk(F_n)\ge\Nk(F_n)\), so \(\Rk(F_n)=O_k(1)\) and \(\Dk(F_n)=\Omega_k(n)\):  \(\BPPk\not\subseteq\Pk\), optimally

three players: improves \(\Omega(n^{1/2})\) [KL25] to \(\Omega(n)\).  \(k\ge4\): previous explicit bound \(\Omega(\log n)\) [BDPW10].  Different function, algebraic rather than combinatorial proof.

The idea in one line

code with good distance  +  hardness of generalized inner product

easy directionan identity between codewords is cheap to test: compare both sides at one random coordinate
hard directionGIP is hard for NOF protocols [BNS92]. We hide a GIP inside the identity and inherit its hardness

nondeterministic lower bounds are very hard to prove for most candidate functions,
so we do not prove a new one:  we reuse the GIP bound

Ingredient 1: code distance and random testing

a linear code \(\WT\subseteq\F_q^{\,r}\) with distance \(\ge\delta r\):
distinct codewords differ in \(\ge\delta r\) coordinates

to test \(u=v\) for \(u,v\in\WT\): pick a random coordinate \(t\in[r]\) and compare \(u(t)\) with \(v(t)\)

\(u\ne v\;\Rightarrow\;\) caught with probability \(\ge\delta\)
the price: one field symbol, \(\log q\) bits

linearity: \(u-v\in\WT\), so a nonzero difference is nonzero on \(\ge\delta r\) coordinates

Random testing on the blackboard

forehead \(i\) carries a codeword \(c^{(i)}\in\WT\).  Test an identity, say \(c^{(1)}+c^{(2)}+c^{(3)}=0\)

protocol: public random \(t\in[r]\); player 2 writes \(c^{(1)}(t)\); player 1 checks \(c^{(1)}(t)+c^{(2)}(t)+c^{(3)}(t)=0\)

cost \(\log q+1\);  true identities always pass; false ones fail with probability \(\ge\delta\)

any identity among codewords is this cheap, if one player can evaluate it coordinate by coordinate

the catch: a linear identity is also easy to certify. We need an identity whose coordinates hide something hard.

Ingredient 2: generalized inner product

\(k\) vectors \(y^{(1)},\ldots,y^{(k)}\in\F_q^{\,w}\), one per forehead

\(\displaystyle\GIP^k_{q,w}(y^{(1)},\ldots,y^{(k)})=\sum_{t=1}^{w}\ \prod_{i=1}^{k} y^{(i)}(t)\)

three players: \(\sum_t x_t\,y_t\,z_t\)

Theorem [BNS92]  \(\Dk(\GIP)=\Omega(w/4^k)\)  over \(\F_q\): [BHK01, BDPW10]

why: the leaves of a NOF protocol are cylinder intersections, and GIP is nearly unbiased on every one of them  next two slides

proof idea: \(k-1\) rounds of Cauchy–Schwarz, each removing one player; what remains is a product of random field elements, exponentially biased towards nothing

Cylinder intersections

inputs \((x,y,z)\): the cube \(\mathcal X_1\times\mathcal X_2\times\mathcal X_3\)

\(A_1\) is a 1-cylinder: membership does not depend on \(x\). A column along the \(x\) axis  the sets player 1, who sees \(y,z\), can decide

\(A_2\): does not depend on \(y\)

\(A_3\): does not depend on \(z\)

cylinder intersection: \(A=A_1\cap A_2\cap A_3\)

the inputs with a given transcript form a cylinder intersection: each message ignores one coordinate. For \(k=2\) these are the rectangles.

The GIP bound

GIP bound [BNS92, BHK01, BDPW10] for every cylinder intersection \(B\subseteq(\F_q^{\,w})^k\) and \(\tau\in\F_q\), under the uniform measure \(\nu\), \[\Bigl|\,\nu\bigl(B\cap\GIP^{-1}(\tau)\bigr)-\tfrac{1}{q}\,\nu(B)\Bigr|\ \le\ 2^{-\Omega_k(w)}\]

GIP is nearly unbiased on every cylinder intersection, however large

what we use: if GIP is constant on \(B\), then \(\nu(B)\le 2^{-\gamma w}\) for a constant \(\gamma=\gamma(k,q)>0\)

plan: combine the easiness of good codes with the hardness of GIP

The function, three players

forehead \(i\) carries \(\ell\) factor vectors \(\ba^{(i)}_1,\ldots,\ba^{(i)}_\ell\in W\) and one vector \(\bc^{(i)}\in\WT\),  all in \(\F_q^{\,r}\)

here \(\ell=2\), \(r=18\); in general \(\ell\) is a constant depending on \(k\)

accept iff \[\sum_{h=1}^{\ell}\ \ba^{(1)}_h\odot\ba^{(2)}_h\odot\ba^{(3)}_h\ =\ \bc^{(1)}+\bc^{(2)}+\bc^{(3)}\] \(\odot\): coordinatewise product in \(\F_q^{\,r}\)

Two ways to read the identity

at one coordinate \(t\): \[\sum_{h}\ \prod_{i}\ba^{(i)}_h(t)\ =\ \sum_i \bc^{(i)}(t)\] one field equation; player 1 can check it given the entries of forehead 1  → the protocol

summed over a set \(S\) of coordinates: \[\sum_{t\in S}\ \sum_{h}\ \prod_{i}\ba^{(i)}_h(t)\] is a GIP of length \(\ell\,|S|\) on the factor entries  → the lower bound

both readings need the right codes

What we need from the codes

1
products stay in the code: \(\ba_1\odot\cdots\odot\ba_k\in\WT\) for all \(\ba_1,\ldots,\ba_k\in W\)
so both sides of the identity lie in \(\WT\)
2
distance: \(\operatorname{dist}(\WT)\ge\delta r\) with \(\delta=\Omega(1)\)
so a false identity fails on \(\ge\delta r\) coordinates
3
dimensions: \(\dim W=\Theta(r)\) and \(\dim\WT=O(\dim W)\)
a long GIP, and 1-inputs that are not too rare
4
constant field: \(q=O_k(1)\)
so one symbol costs \(O_k(1)\) bits

Reed–Solomon gives \(\Rk=O_k(\log n)\) and \(\Nk=\Omega_k(n)\): enough for \(\BPPk\not\subseteq\NPk\), not for constant cost

Reed–Solomon: \(W\) = polynomials of degree \(<r/2k\), \(\WT\) = degree \(<r/2\), evaluated at \(r\) points of \(\F_q\)

1 degrees add   2 distance \(\ge r/2\)   3 \(\dim\WT\le k\dim W\)

4 needs \(q\ge r\): a symbol costs \(\log q=\Theta(\log n)\) bits

Algebraic geometry codes

the same property over a fixed field [Couvreur22, Rand15]: evaluate functions on a curve with many rational points instead of polynomials on a line

Theorem [Garcia–Stichtenoth 96, Shum et al. 01] Let \(q\) be a sufficiently large power of \(4\) and \(r_j=(q-\sqrt q)\,q^{j/2}\). There are linear codes \(W_j,\WT_j\subseteq\F_q^{\,r_j}\) with \(W_j^{\odot k}\subseteq\WT_j\) for every \(k\le\sqrt q/32\),  \(\operatorname{dist}(\WT_j)\ge 3r_j/4\),  \(6r_j/\sqrt q\le\dim W_j\le 8r_j/\sqrt q\),  \(\dim\WT_j\le r_j/4\), constructible and encodable in \(\operatorname{poly}(r_j)\) time.
Reed–SolomonGarcia–Stichtenoth field size\(q\ge r\)\(q=\Theta(k^2)\) one symbol\(\Theta(\log n)\) bits\(O(\log k)\) bits randomized cost\(O_k(\log n)\)\(O_k(1)\)

from now on \(q=\Theta(k^2)\) is a constant;  \(m=\dim W=\Theta_k(r)\),  \(\widetilde m=\dim\WT\le r/4\)

The constant-cost protocol

1. public random coordinate \(t\in[r]\)

2. player 2 writes \(\ba^{(1)}_1(t),\ldots,\ba^{(1)}_\ell(t),\ \bc^{(1)}(t)\): the \(\ell+1\) symbols hidden from player 1

3. player 1 checks \(\sum_h\prod_i\ba^{(i)}_h(t)=\sum_i\bc^{(i)}(t)\) and announces the bit

analysis: \(\mathbf b:=\sum_h\ba^{(1)}_h\odot\cdots\odot\ba^{(k)}_h-\sum_i\bc^{(i)}\in\WT\)
1-input: \(\mathbf b=0\), always accepted
0-input: \(\mathbf b\ne0\), so \(\mathbf b(t)\ne0\) with probability \(\ge3/4\)
cost \((\ell+1)\log q+1=O_k(1)\)

total: the input bits are the coefficients of the codewords in fixed bases, \(n=(\ell m+\widetilde m)\log q\); every bit string is an input

The lower bound: what to show

Fact [BDPW10] a nondeterministic protocol of cost \(d\) covers \(F^{-1}(1)\) by at most \(2^d\) accepting cylinder intersections

why: fix a certificate and a transcript; the inputs consistent with them form a cylinder intersection, and all of them are accepted. A cover, not a partition: the pieces may overlap

plan, with \(\mu\) uniform on inputs, \(m=\dim W\), \(\widetilde m=\dim\WT\):

(a) every accepting cylinder intersection \(A\) has \(\mu(A)\le 2^{-\gamma\ell m}\)

(b) the 1-inputs have \(\mu(F^{-1}(1))=q^{-\widetilde m}\)

then \(2^d\cdot 2^{-\gamma\ell m}\ \ge\ q^{-\widetilde m}\),  so \(d\ \ge\ \gamma\ell m-\widetilde m\log q\)

Information sets

an information set of \(W\): \(S\subseteq[r]\) with \(|S|=m=\dim W\) such that \(\ba\mapsto\ba|_S\) is a bijection \(W\to\F_q^{\,S}\)

exists: take \(m\) independent columns of a generator matrix

the values on \(S\) are free, and they determine the codeword

so the \(\ell\) factors on forehead \(i\) are the same thing as an unrestricted vector \[y^{(i)}:=\bigl(\ba^{(i)}_1|_S,\ldots,\ba^{(i)}_\ell|_S\bigr)\in\F_q^{\,\ell m},\] uniform when the codewords are

Accepting sets hide a GIP

fix \(\bc^{(1)},\ldots,\bc^{(k)}\) and sum the identity over \(S\):

\[\underbrace{\sum_{t\in S}\sum_{h=1}^{\ell}\prod_{i=1}^{k}\ba^{(i)}_h(t)}_{\GIP^{k}_{q,\ell m}(y^{(1)},\ldots,y^{(k)})}\ =\ \underbrace{\sum_{t\in S}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\bc^{(i)}(t)}_{=:\ \tau}\]

on every 1-input with these \(\bc^{(i)}\):  \(\GIP(y)=\tau\)

Lemma. \(A\) accepting cylinder intersection, \(\bc\) fixed.  Its slice \(B=\{y:(y,\bc)\in A\}\subseteq(\F_q^{\,\ell m})^k\) is a cylinder intersection,  \(B\subseteq\GIP^{-1}(\tau)\),  \(\nu(B)=\mu(A\mid\bc)\)

GIP bound: \(\nu(B)\le 2^{-\gamma\ell m}\)

average over \(\bc\):  \(\mu(A)\le 2^{-\gamma\ell m}\)  — that is (a)

How many 1-inputs?

fix all factors \(\ba^{(i)}_h\) and \(\bc^{(1)},\ldots,\bc^{(k-1)}\)

the identity reads \[\bc^{(k)}\ =\ \sum_{h}\ba^{(1)}_h\odot\cdots\odot\ba^{(k)}_h\ -\ \sum_{i<k}\bc^{(i)}\]

the right-hand side lies in \(\WT\): products stay in \(\WT\), and \(\WT\) is linear
so exactly one \(\bc^{(k)}\in\WT\) works

\(\mu(F^{-1}(1))=1/|\WT|=q^{-\widetilde m}\)  — that is (b), and it does not depend on \(\ell\)

Putting it together

\(\displaystyle q^{-\widetilde m}\ =\ \mu\bigl(F^{-1}(1)\bigr)\ \le\ \sum_{a\le 2^d}\mu\bigl(A^{(a)}\bigr)\ \le\ 2^{d}\cdot 2^{-\gamma\ell m}\)

\(\displaystyle d\ \ge\ \gamma\,\ell\,m\ -\ \widetilde m\log q\)

the point: the density of the 1-inputs does not depend on \(\ell\), whereas the GIP bound strengthens as \(\ell\) grows

\(\widetilde m\le r/4\) and \(m\ge 6r/\sqrt q\), so a constant \(\ell=\ell(k)\) makes \(\gamma\ell m\ge 2\widetilde m\log q\),  and \(d\ge\tfrac12\gamma\ell m=\Omega_k(m)\)

each forehead holds \(n=(\ell m+\widetilde m)\log q=\Theta_k(m)\) bits:  \(\Nk(F_n)=\Omega_k(n)\)  ∎

Summary

an explicit total \(F_n\) with \(\Rk(F_n)=O_k(1)\) and \(\Nk(F_n)=\Omega_k(n)\) for every fixed \(k\ge3\):  \(\BPPk\not\subseteq\NPk\), \(\BPPk\not\subseteq\Pk\)

the recipe: hide GIP inside an identity between codewords.  The code makes the identity cheap to test; the GIP makes it hard to certify.

codes: Reed–Solomon already gives \(O_k(\log n)\) vs \(\Omega_k(n)\); algebraic geometry codes bring the randomized cost to a constant

the lower bound is inherited, not proved from scratch: an information set turns accepting cylinder intersections into GIP-constant ones

what next? other hard functions hidden in coded identities; other separations with the same recipe

Thank you.
\(\Rk(F_n)=O_k(1),\qquad \Nk(F_n)=\Omega_k(n)\)
